snip.t: Group 3: PH due to Lung Diseases and/or Hypoxia — COPD, interstitial lung disease (ILD), chronic high altitude exposure, obstructive sleep apnoea, TB sequelae (fibrosis, bronchiectasis)

Airway‑breathing‑circulation – obese patients may have obstructive sleep‑apnoea (OSA) or hypoventilation; ensure supine positioning with head‑of‑bed elevation, give supplemental O₂ if SpO₂ < 94 % and consider non‑invasive ventilation for acute hypercapnic respiratory failure.
Respiratory: Obstructive sleep‑apnoea, obesity hypoventilation syndrome — Daytime somnolence, pulmonary hypertension

Complications: type 2 diabetes and insulin resistance (acanthosis nigricans), hypertension, dyslipidaemia, fatty liver disease, obstructive sleep apnoea, slipped upper femoral epiphysis and knee pain, early puberty, and psychological problems.
